outcome: Model-view-controller restoration complete: page modules drive the simulator and results through controller commands, and page events follow one documented naming scheme
owner_impact: Nothing changes on screen. Before, several parts of the page operated the simulator by pressing its hidden old buttons: the Library's Open & run, the Showcase auto-run, the automatic pause when result saving falls behind, the Metrics apply, and loading an Experiment's sources. The saved results layout was applied the same way, by pressing hidden plot buttons. They now call the simulation and results controllers directly, and those controllers refuse exactly when the buttons were disabled. The simulator's status (starting, ready, error) is now part of the runtime model, so the React status badge and the accessibility busy flag read it from the model instead of watching the status text. Internal page events now all use one naming scheme and are documented in one table, with a test that fails if an event is sent that nothing listens to, or the reverse. That test found five events nobody listened to and one listener nothing sent (left over from the old Professor supervision dialog), and those were removed. Test now: optional. Open an Experiment from the Library with Open & run, run and pause, apply a Metrics edit while running, and check the simulator badge; everything should behave as before.

next.text: The owner-approved four-stage model-view-controller plan (#560 runtime model, #562 simulation controller, #564 results and authoring models, #567 authoring controller, #569 retiring duplicate views and watchers) is complete, and #569 is closed. Each panel now has one model holding its state, one controller owning its rules and commands, and views that only draw the model and call commands. The refactoring epic #425 stays open for future tickets. The live Lab behaves as before and is available to use.

technical_evidence: Runtime model gains simulatorStatus {state,text}; main.js writes it through showSimulatorStatus (a message without a state keeps the previous state, as before). The React readiness badge reads it through the adapter snapshot; ux-hardening's aria-busy subscribes to it (microtask-deferred, like the attribute observer it replaces). The unused boundaryLabel read of another module's badge text is removed.

Hidden-button clicks replaced by commands: experiment-library (Open & run), showcase (auto-run), result-persistence (backpressure pause), metrics-runtime-bridge (pause before Metrics apply), registry-ui-v3 (apply loaded sources; readiness wait reads controls.applySources). results-presentation-bridge clears plots with resultsCommands.removePanel over resultsModel panels and adds with the new resultsCommands.addPanelWithMetrics.

Events: vlab-open-experiment-library and vlab-refresh-experiment-library renamed to the vlab: prefix; dead listener vlab:open-supervised-experiment and unheard vlab:metrics-applied, vlab:metrics-error, vlab:runtime-ready and vlab-experiment-library-bridge-ready removed. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 19 documents models, controllers and every page event; new page-events.test.mjs enforces prefix, pairing and documentation.

A/B against main's production build (mirrored libraries): results, editor and 28 apply scenarios byte-identical; simulation identical once the timing-dependent pause counters are masked; new readiness timeline harness identical in its settled states (5 ms start-up frames vary between runs of either build; one old run matched the new byte for byte). Fallback view with React blocked works; full browser smoke passes; style comparison identical at all four viewports; 690 tests pass; typecheck clean.
